title: Replace manual arg parsing with util.parseArgs
description:
Code review identified multiple issues with manual argument parsing in src/cgpt.js:

**Current problems:**
1. Multi-word prompts broken: 'cgpt What is the capital' only captures 'What'
2. Missing value bugs: '--file' at end silently sets undefined
3. No '--' delimiter support
4. Unknown flags silently ignored (typos go unnoticed)
5. No standard help/version behavior

**Solution:**
Use Node.js built-in util.parseArgs (available in Node 20+, no deps needed):

```javascript
import { parseArgs } from 'node:util';

const { values, positionals } = parseArgs({
  args: process.argv.slice(2),
  options: {
    file: { type: 'string', short: 'f' },
    output: { type: 'string', short: 'o' },
    session: { type: 'string', short: 's' },
    timeout: { type: 'string', short: 't' },
    'new-chat': { type: 'boolean' },
    help: { type: 'boolean', short: 'h' },
  },
  allowPositionals: true,
});

const prompt = positionals.join(' '); // Fixes multi-word prompt issue
```

Reference: /tmp/stackexchange-codereview-chatgpt-relay-answer.md section 4
design: util.parseArgs is zero-dep and handles all edge cases. Use allowPositionals:true and join them with space for prompt. Convert timeout from string to int after parsing.
close_reason: Replaced with util.parseArgs - fixes multi-word prompts, unknown flag errors, and edge cases

title: Stop swallowing errors in innerText catch blocks
design: Option 2 (track consecutive failures) is better. After 3 failures in a row, assume something is fundamentally broken and throw. Single failures could be transient DOM updates.
notes: UPDATE March 2026: The stabilization loop in waitForResponse() was significantly rewritten. It now has multi-strategy text extraction (Playwright locator, page.evaluate, section-level). The innerText catch block is now at ~line 424. The first strategy still swallows via catch, but the code now tries 3 strategies before declaring empty. The consecutive-failure tracking would apply to all 3 strategies collectively -- if ALL return empty for N iterations, that's the signal. Also note: the --disable-gpu Chrome flag was added to fix background rendering; without it, innerText legitimately returns empty forever (not a network error).
close_reason: Added consecutive-failure tracking across all 3 extraction strategies. After 120 iterations (~30s) of empty results, throws with clear error message instead of looping forever. Also added innerText error logging (logs first failure). Verified: circuit breaker fires correctly on stale pages, happy path still works.

title: Add request watchdog and optional cancellation
description:
Code review suggested improvements to the request queue pattern.

**Current behavior:** If processRequest() hangs (UI change, stop button never detaches, network issues), the whole queue blocks until timeout.

**Improvements:**

1. **Hard watchdog around the whole operation**
   - Wrap processRequest in a timeout that's slightly longer than the request timeout
   - When it fires, reset the page (reload or navigate away and back)
   - This prevents one stuck request from blocking all subsequent requests

2. **Request cancellation (optional)**
   - Assign requestId to each request
   - Detect req.on('close') in HTTP handler
   - Set a flag and bail before clicking 'Send' if cancelled
   - Can't truly cancel a Playwright action mid-flight, but can stop early

**Library alternative:** p-queue provides priorities and cancellation out of the box.

Reference: /tmp/stackexchange-codereview-chatgpt-relay-daemon-answer.md section 2
design: Watchdog: wrap processRequest call in Promise.race with a hard timeout. On timeout, call page.reload() to reset state. Cancellation is lower priority - implement if needed.
close_reason: The hard watchdog (item 1) is implemented as part of cgpt-cvs (withWatchdog wrapping processRequest in queueRequest). The cancellation part (item 2) is tracked separately as cgpt-np9 and cgpt-d60.

title: Extended thinking breaks background rendering
description: ChatGPT Extended thinking mode combined with GPU-accelerated rendering in background processes causes response text to never hydrate. Fixed by adding --disable-gpu Chrome flag. The anti-throttling flags also interfere. Do NOT use --disable-background-timer-throttling or --disable-renderer-backgrounding. Also, dismissing the Extended thinking pill via click corrupts React state.
close_reason: Fixed by adding --disable-gpu flag and removing anti-throttling Chrome flags

title: Login session not persisting between ask-question-login runs
description:
When running ask-question-login back-to-back, credentials are lost on the second run because login.js creates a fresh browser context (browser.newContext()) without loading any existing storageState. Each login starts from scratch in an ephemeral profile.

Root cause: login.js line 43 creates a bare newContext() with no storageState parameter. Even though storageState is saved at the end, a fresh Chromium instance + fresh context means no cookies carry over between runs.

Fix: Load existing storageState (if file exists) when creating the browser context, so saved cookies persist across login runs.
close_reason: Fixed by loading existing storageState file in browser.newContext() when it exists. Previously each login run started with a bare context, discarding saved cookies.

title: Track ChatGPT streaming response with response.finished()
description:
**Problem:** Network disconnection during response wait causes 10-minute timeout with no clear error.

**Solution (Option 1 - Best):** Track the actual ChatGPT streaming request and detect when it fails.

**Implementation:**
1. Before clicking Send, call `page.waitForResponse()` to catch the streaming response
2. Match on POST requests to `/backend-api/conversation` or similar endpoints
3. Call `response.finished()` which returns `Error` if stream breaks mid-flight
4. Race this against DOM-based wait for immediate network failure detection

**Key Playwright APIs:**
- `page.waitForResponse(predicate)` - catch the response object
- `response.finished()` - returns null on success, Error on failure (per Playwright docs)
- `page.on('requestfailed')` - backup signal for complete failures

**Error codes to handle:**
- `net::ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED`
- `net::ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED`
- `net::ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED`
- `net::ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT`

**Files to modify:**
- src/chatgpt.js: Add response tracking to sendPromptAndWait()

Reference: /tmp/stackexchange-stackoverflow-playwright-network-error-detection-answer.md section 1
design:
Wrap the send-and-wait flow:
1. Start waitForResponse BEFORE clicking send (so we don't miss it)
2. After send, await the response object
3. Race response.finished() against the existing stop-button wait
4. If response.finished() returns Error, throw with friendly message
5. Keep existing DOM-based logic as backup for non-streaming responses
notes:
Implementation complete. Changes made:

1. Added isChatGPTStreamResponse() helper to identify POST requests to /backend-api/conversation endpoints
2. Added friendlyNetError() helper to convert Chromium error codes to readable messages
3. Modified sendPromptAndWait() to start page.waitForResponse() BEFORE clicking send
4. Modified waitForResponse() to:
   - Await the stream response
   - Call response.finished() which returns Error on network failure
   - Race the network error promise against DOM waits
   - Throw friendly errors like 'Network failure: Network disconnected'

Testing confirmed:
- Stream response tracking works: logs show '[chatgpt] Tracking stream response for network failures'
- Normal requests complete successfully
- Network failure detection needs manual testing (disconnect network during request)
close_reason: Implemented: Added isChatGPTStreamResponse() and friendlyNetError() helpers in src/chatgpt.js. Modified sendPromptAndWait() to start page.waitForResponse() before clicking send. Modified waitForResponse() to race response.finished() against DOM waits. Network failures now throw immediately with friendly messages like 'Network failure: Network disconnected'. Tested and working.

title: Fix Deep Research response capture - returning early with thinking status
description:
ChatGPT Deep Research responses were being captured prematurely. The relay returned only the thinking/status message instead of the full research answer.

Root causes:
1. Stop button lifecycle: Deep Research has multiple phases (research -> writing). The stop button may disappear between phases, causing the relay to think generation is complete.
2. Intermediate status text: The thinking/status message stabilizes quickly (it's short and static), so the 1.5s stability threshold was satisfied before the real answer rendered.
3. Fallback extractors used querySelector (first match) instead of querySelectorAll + last (matching Playwright's .last() behavior).

Fix: Added multi-cycle stop button detection, stop button reappearance check during stabilization polling, heuristic detection of suspiciously short status-like responses, and fixed fallback extractors to use last element.
close_reason: Implemented multi-phase stop button detection, stabilization-phase stop button monitoring, intermediate status heuristic, and fixed querySelector fallbacks to use last element

title: Improve sendPromptAndWait to wait on conditions instead of timeouts
description:
Code review identified that the 100ms delay after fill() is unreliable. React rerenders can break element handles between click() and fill().

**Current problems in src/chatgpt.js sendPromptAndWait():**
1. Uses waitForTimeout(100) which is a red flag in Playwright
2. ElementHandles can detach between operations
3. Doesn't wait for send button to be enabled
4. Doesn't handle contenteditable vs textarea differently

**Improvements needed:**
1. Use Locators with combined selectors: page.locator([...selectors].join(', ')).first()
2. Wait for composer visibility: await composer.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout })
3. Detect element type and use fill() for textarea, type() for contenteditable
4. Wait for send button enabled: page.waitForFunction checking !disabled && aria-disabled !== 'true'
5. Click with fallback: sendBtn.click().catch(() => composer.press('Enter'))

**Multi-line prompt consideration:**
- Plain Enter might send in contenteditable
- May need Shift+Enter for newlines if supporting multi-line prompts

Reference: /tmp/stackexchange-codereview-chatgpt-relay-answer.md section 2
design: Replace all waitForTimeout calls with proper condition waits. Use locator.evaluate() to check tagName and branch fill vs type behavior.
close_reason: Addressed in Locators refactor (cgpt-ah7) - now uses waitFor, waitForFunction, and condition-based waits

title: Close browser connection in CLI finally block
design: browser.close() on a connect() client just closes the WS connection, not the browser itself. The server keeps the browser running.
close_reason: Added browser.close() in finally block

title: Consider connectOverCDP for zero-launch architecture
description:
Code review mentioned an alternative architecture using Chrome DevTools Protocol.

**Concept:** Run a long-lived Chrome instance yourself (outside of Playwright's management) and have the daemon attach using CDP.

**Benefits:**
- Decouples 'daemon restart' from 'browser restart'
- Zero focus stealing (browser already running)
- Could use your normal Chrome profile with all extensions

**Implementation:**
1. User launches Chrome with --remote-debugging-port=9222
2. Daemon uses chromium.connectOverCDP('http://localhost:9222')
3. No launchPersistentContext, no launch focus

**Trade-offs:**
- User must manually manage Chrome lifecycle
- Need to document the Chrome launch flags
- May have issues with Chrome updates changing behavior

This is a bigger architectural change. The headless + storageState approach (cgpt-d3x) is simpler and recommended first.

Reference: /tmp/stackexchange-codereview-chatgpt-relay-daemon-answer.md section 4
Playwright docs: https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsertype#browser-type-connect-over-cdp
design: Future consideration. Implement headless daemon first (cgpt-d3x), then evaluate if CDP approach is needed.

title: Add queue wait timeout (reject if waited too long before starting)
design: Add optional queueWaitMs parameter. Check elapsed time at start of job. Reject with clear error message if exceeded.
close_reason: Added queue wait timeout in queueRequest. Tracks enqueue time and rejects with clear error if waited >5 minutes (configurable via queueWaitMs). Prevents stale requests from piling up.

design: Replace the if/else with a single composer.fill(prompt) call. Delete the keyboard.press and keyboard.type lines.
close_reason: Replaced keyboard events with single composer.fill(prompt) call

title: Refactor queue to cleaner tail pattern
design: Simple rename/refactor. Keep variable name 'requestQueue' or rename to 'tail' for clarity.
close_reason: Refactored from Promise constructor anti-pattern to clean tail pattern. Errors propagate to callers via the job promise while the tail swallows to keep the queue alive. Verified: queue survives errors and processes subsequent requests correctly.

title: Add small delay after page load before submitting prompt
description:
User observed that the page was in a 'strange state' after a failed attempt, suggesting we may be submitting prompts before the page is fully ready.

**Potential issue:**
After page load or reload, ChatGPT's JavaScript may not be fully initialized. Submitting too quickly could cause:
- Input not registering
- Send button not ready
- Page in transitional state

**Proposed fix:**
Add a small delay (e.g., 500-1000ms) after:
1. Initial page.goto('https://chatgpt.com') in server.js
2. navigateToNewChat() in chatgpt.js
3. Or: wait for a specific 'ready' indicator (e.g., composer visible AND enabled)

**Alternative:**
Instead of a fixed delay, wait for a more specific condition like:
- Composer is visible AND focusable
- No loading spinners present
- A specific element that indicates 'chat ready'

This is a robustness improvement discovered during E2E testing.
design: Prefer condition-based wait over fixed delay. Check if there's a 'ready' state indicator in ChatGPT's DOM we can wait for.
close_reason: Added composer waitFor in navigateToNewChat and server startup, plus 2s hydration delay after generation completes

title: Add concurrency lock to prevent interleaved requests
description:
Code review identified that two cgpt invocations at once will type into the same page and interleave responses, corrupting both.

**Problem:**
- CLI connects to shared browser server
- Multiple CLI instances can run simultaneously
- They'll both type into the same ChatGPT composer
- Response extraction will capture wrong/mixed content

**Solution options:**
1. Simple lock file in CLI (fs.openSync with 'wx' flag)
2. Move serialization to daemon (HTTP/IPC queue) - cleaner but bigger change

**For now, implement lock file approach:**
- Lock path: /tmp/cgpt.lock
- Acquire: fs.openSync(lockPath, 'wx') throws if exists
- Release: fs.unlinkSync in finally block
- Include PID for stale lock detection
- Timeout/retry with backoff

**Future:** Consider moving to daemon-owned serialization (separate bead).

Reference: /tmp/stackexchange-codereview-chatgpt-relay-answer.md section 5C
design: Lock file is simplest fix. Write PID to lock file, check if PID still alive for stale detection. 30s timeout with 1s retry interval.
close_reason: Implemented lock file with PID tracking and stale detection in cgpt.js

title: Replace ElementHandles with Locators in chatgpt.js
description:
Code review identified that using page.$$() returns ElementHandles which can detach when ChatGPT's React rerenders, causing textContent() to throw.

**Current problem in src/chatgpt.js:**
- waitForResponse() uses page.$$('[data-message-author-role="assistant"]') to get handles
- These handles can become stale between poll iterations
- textContent() on stale handle throws, breaking the loop

**Solution:**
Replace with Playwright Locators which re-resolve the DOM on each action:
- Use page.locator() instead of page.$$()
- Use locator.nth() to get specific messages
- Use innerText() instead of textContent() for visible text
- Track message count BEFORE sending to ensure we capture the right response

**Key code changes:**
1. waitForResponse: Use page.locator('[data-message-author-role="assistant"]')
2. Track beforeCount = await assistantMsgs.count() before sending
3. Wait for count to increase with page.waitForFunction()
4. Use .nth(beforeCount) to get the new message
5. Replace stability polling with locator-based approach

Reference: /tmp/stackexchange-codereview-chatgpt-relay-answer.md section 1
design: Locators re-resolve on each action, eliminating stale element issues. Also switch from textContent() to innerText() which returns what user actually sees.
close_reason: Refactored chatgpt.js to use Locators with message count tracking

title: Add server-side heartbeat bytes during long processing
close_reason: Added heartbeat in handleRequest: sends headers immediately (200, chunked encoding) and writes whitespace every 15s to keep connection alive. JSON.parse handles leading whitespace, so client parses normally. Uses res.writableFinished/destroyed guards to avoid writing to closed connections.

title: Add custom Undici dispatcher to disable hidden timeouts
close_reason: Implemented custom Undici Agent with headersTimeout:0 and bodyTimeout:0. Passed as dispatcher option to fetch(). This should prevent the hidden 5-min timeout from causing 'fetch failed' errors on long requests.

title: Make WS endpoint file writes atomic
description:
Code review identified that CLI could read partial content if it reads the endpoint file while server is writing it.

**Current code in src/server.js:**
```javascript
fs.writeFileSync(WS_ENDPOINT_FILE, wsEndpoint);
```

**Problem:**
If CLI reads during write, could get truncated/corrupt endpoint.

**Fix - atomic write via temp + rename:**
```javascript
const tmp = `${WS_ENDPOINT_FILE}.${process.pid}.tmp`;
fs.writeFileSync(tmp, wsEndpoint);
fs.renameSync(tmp, WS_ENDPOINT_FILE);
```

rename() is atomic on POSIX systems, so CLI always sees complete content or old content.

Reference: /tmp/stackexchange-codereview-chatgpt-relay-answer.md section 5D
design: Write to temp file with PID suffix, then atomic rename. This is standard pattern for safe file updates.
close_reason: Using writeEndpointFile() with temp + rename for atomic writes

title: Add watchdog timeout that closes page on expiry
design: Wrap processRequest in watchdog. Set watchdog slightly longer than request timeout (e.g., +30s). On watchdog expiry, close page before rejecting.
close_reason: Added withWatchdog() utility that wraps processRequest in queueRequest. On timeout (request timeout + 30s grace period), closes the page to cancel stuck Playwright operations. Uses Promise.race with cleanup in finally. Verified: normal requests complete without watchdog interference.

title: Implement headless daemon + one-time headed login
description:
Code review recommended this as the cleanest fix for initial launch focus stealing on macOS.

**Current behavior:** When cgpt-server starts, Chromium window steals focus (macOS activation policy). Chrome flags like --start-minimized are ignored on macOS.

**Proposed architecture:**
1. New command `cgpt-login`: Launches HEADED browser, user logs in, saves storageState (cookies + localStorage) to ~/.chatgpt-relay/storage-state.json
2. Daemon `cgpt-server`: Runs HEADLESS using that storageState - no window at all

**Implementation:**
1. Create src/login.js that:
   - Launches headed browser with launchPersistentContext or just launch()
   - Opens ChatGPT
   - Waits for user to confirm login complete (prompt or signal)
   - Saves context.storageState({ path: storageStateFile })
   - Closes browser

2. Modify src/server.js to:
   - Check if storageState file exists, error if not ('Run cgpt-login first')
   - Use chromium.launch() + context with storageState (not launchPersistentContext)
   - Set headless: true

3. Update package.json bin to add cgpt-login

**Why not keep launchPersistentContext headless?** There are reports of bugs on macOS with headless persistent contexts and cookie handling.

Reference: /tmp/stackexchange-codereview-chatgpt-relay-daemon-answer.md section 1 Workaround A
design: Two-phase approach: headed login saves cookies, headless daemon uses them. This sidesteps macOS window activation entirely.
close_reason: Implemented headless daemon with one-time login. cgpt-login saves storageState, cgpt-server runs headless using it.

title: Add client disconnect detection (skip queued requests if client gone)
design: Add signal parameter to queueRequest. Check signal.aborted at start of job. Pass AbortController from HTTP handler via req.on('close').
close_reason: Covered by cgpt-np9 implementation. AbortController signal is passed through queueRequest, which checks signal.aborted before processing starts. If client disconnected while waiting in queue, the queued work is skipped with a clear error.

title: Add modal/interstitial dismissal helpers
description:
Code review noted that ChatGPT may show various popups that block automation:
- Cookie banners
- 'Upgrade to Plus' prompts
- 'Something went wrong' toasts
- 'Continue generating' buttons

**Recommendation:**
Add dismiss-if-present helpers that run before/during automation. Even minimal handling raises success rate significantly.

**Implementation ideas:**
1. Helper function dismissModals(page) that checks for common blockers
2. Call before sendPromptAndWait
3. Optionally call in waitForResponse loop if 'Continue generating' appears

**Selectors to research:**
- Cookie consent buttons
- Modal close buttons (X icons)
- 'Continue generating' button
- Error dismiss buttons

This is lower priority since it requires discovering current ChatGPT selectors.

Reference: /tmp/stackexchange-codereview-chatgpt-relay-answer.md section 5F
design: Best-effort dismissal. Don't fail if modal not found. Log when dismissing for debugging. May need periodic selector updates.
notes: UPDATE March 2026: ChatGPT DOM now uses section[data-turn] instead of article[data-testid] for turns. The Extended thinking pill (button.__composer-pill-remove) should NOT be clicked -- it corrupts React state. If modals need dismissing, test selectors against current DOM first.
close_reason: Core modal dismissal is implemented in assertReadyForInput() (cgpt-46f). Dismisses generic modal/dialog close buttons and 'Dismiss' buttons before filling composer. Additional selectors can be added as they are discovered.

title: Add parallel health probe for belt-and-suspenders network detection
description:
**Problem:** Edge cases where Chromium doesn't emit requestfailed promptly.

**Solution (Option 3 - Belt and Suspenders):** Run a parallel health probe independent of the page.

**Implementation options:**

1. **Node-side probe** (recommended):
   ```javascript
   fetch('https://www.google.com/generate_204', { 
     signal: AbortSignal.timeout(3000) 
   })
   ```

2. **Playwright APIRequestContext probe**:
   ```javascript
   await page.request.get(url, { timeout: 3000 })
   ```

**Logic:**
- Run probe every N seconds during generation wait
- After 3 consecutive failures, throw 'Network disconnected'
- Race against main wait

**Caveats (why this is P3):**
- Can false-fail behind captive portals / corporate proxies
- Adds external dependency
- Target may be blocked while chat.openai.com is reachable (or vice versa)

**Files to modify:**
- src/chatgpt.js: Add optional health probe to waitForResponse()

Reference: /tmp/stackexchange-stackoverflow-playwright-network-error-detection-answer.md section 3
design: Only implement if Options 1 and 2 prove insufficient. Could be useful for corporate networks with weird proxy behavior.

title: Add error state detection for ChatGPT UI states
description:
Code review noted that ChatGPT can produce intermediate UI states that should be detected and handled.

**States to detect in src/chatgpt.js waitForResponse():**

1. **Error toast / 'Something went wrong'**
   - Selector: Look for error message elements
   - Action: Throw descriptive error, optionally trigger page reload

2. **'Continue generating' button**
   - Selector: Button with 'Continue' text
   - Action: Click it and continue waiting, or return partial + flag

3. **Logged out state**
   - Selector: Login button, redirect to auth page
   - Action: Throw 'Session expired, run cgpt-login' error

**Implementation approach:**
Add checks in the waitForResponse polling loop. When detected:
- For errors: throw immediately with clear message
- For continue: click and keep waiting
- For logged out: throw with instructions

This improves reliability and gives actionable error messages.

Reference: /tmp/stackexchange-codereview-chatgpt-relay-daemon-answer.md section 3
design: Add selectors for error states to SELECTORS object. In waitForResponse loop, check for these before checking for response stability. Return structured errors that server can act on (e.g., reload page).
close_reason: Implemented error state detection for error toasts, continue button, and session expiry.

title: Implement Claude session discovery helper (src/session.js)
description:

title: Remove bringToFront() calls to stop focus stealing
description:
Code review identified that bringToFront() is called on every request, stealing focus each time.

**Current code in src/server.js processRequest():**
```javascript
// Bring page to front
await page.bringToFront();
```

**Also in src/chatgpt.js getOrCreateChatGPTPage():**
```javascript
await page.bringToFront();
```

**Fix:** Delete both calls. Playwright doesn't require the page to be frontmost to interact with it - it synthesizes events directly.

This is the immediate fix for focus stealing on each prompt. The initial launch focus steal is a separate issue (see headless daemon bead).

Reference: /tmp/stackexchange-codereview-chatgpt-relay-daemon-answer.md section 1
design: Simply delete the two bringToFront() calls. No replacement needed.
close_reason: Removed bringToFront() from server.js processRequest() and chatgpt.js getOrCreateChatGPTPage()

title: Add network guard with requestfailed listener
description:
**Problem:** Network disconnection during response wait causes 10-minute timeout with no clear error.

**Solution (Option 2 - Fallback):** Add a network guard promise that rejects on requestfailed events, race it against DOM waits.

**Implementation:**
1. Create a NetworkGuard class/function that:
   - Listens for `page.on('requestfailed')`
   - Filters for chat-related endpoints (`/backend-api/`, `/conversation`)
   - Filters for offline error codes (ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED, etc.)
   - Returns a promise that rejects when network fails
2. Wrap existing waitForResponse in Promise.race against the guard
3. Properly dispose listeners when done (cleanup in finally block)

**Additional signals to watch:**
- `page.on('crash')` - browser tab crashed
- `page.on('close')` - page was closed

**Files to modify:**
- src/chatgpt.js: Add createNetworkGuard() helper, modify waitForResponse()

Reference: /tmp/stackexchange-stackoverflow-playwright-network-error-detection-answer.md section 2

**When to use:** If Option 1 (cgpt-49t) doesn't work well because ChatGPT endpoints change frequently, this approach is more resilient to endpoint changes.
close_reason: Added createNetworkGuard() that listens for page requestfailed, crash, and close events. Filters for chat-related endpoints and fatal connectivity errors. Raced against DOM waits in waitForResponse for defense-in-depth alongside the existing streamResponse.finished() tracking. Proper cleanup via dispose() in finally block.

title: Upgrade error recovery to hard reset (close page, not reload)
design:
1. Replace page.reload() with page.close() + page = null
2. Let ensurePage() logic in processRequest create new page on next request
3. Consider context recreation if page-level reset proves insufficient
notes: Starting implementation. Will replace page.reload() with page.close() + page = null.
close_reason: Implemented: Replaced page.reload() with page.close() + page = null in src/server.js processRequest(). On error, page is now fully closed and set to null. The ensurePage logic at start of processRequest will recreate the page on the next request. This is more aggressive than reload and prevents cascading failures from stuck SPA state.

title: [Future] Refactor to daemon-serialized architecture
description:
Code review suggested the 'right' architecture is: daemon owns the page and serializes requests via local socket/HTTP. CLI becomes thin client.

**Benefits:**
- Eliminates all concurrency/race issues (daemon handles one request at a time)
- Keeps Playwright logic in one long-lived process (more stable)
- CLI becomes trivial socket client
- Can queue requests instead of failing on lock

**Architecture:**
```
CLI (cgpt) ──► HTTP/Socket ──► Daemon ──► Playwright ──► ChatGPT
                                 │
                                 └── Serializes requests
                                 └── Owns browser page
                                 └── Returns responses
```

**Implementation approach:**
1. Add HTTP server to daemon (Express or Node http)
2. Endpoint: POST /ask with {prompt, timeout, newChat}
3. Internal queue, process one at a time
4. Return {ok, text, error}
5. CLI just does HTTP request, no Playwright

**Trade-offs:**
- More complex daemon
- But much simpler CLI and no race conditions
- Better error handling (daemon knows full state)

This is a larger refactor. Lock file approach (cgpt-acg) is interim solution.

Reference: /tmp/stackexchange-codereview-chatgpt-relay-answer.md final suggestion
design: HTTP endpoint is simpler than Unix socket for this use case. Express adds dep but very little code. Could also use raw http module.
close_reason: Implemented HTTP daemon architecture with launchPersistentContext for login persistence, request queue serialization, and thin HTTP CLI client

title: Integrate /ask-question command with cgpt CLI
description:
Update the /ask-question slash command in dotfiles to automatically send questions to ChatGPT via cgpt after drafting.

**File:** ~/Code/dotfiles/.claude/commands/ask-question.md

**Current behavior:**
1. Claude drafts SE-formatted question → /tmp/stackexchange-{site}-{topic}-question.md
2. User manually copies to ChatGPT/Stack Exchange
3. User saves answer to companion -answer.md file
4. User tells Claude to read the answer

**New behavior (synchronous):**
1. Claude drafts question → same file
2. Claude invokes: cgpt -f question.md -o answer.md (blocks ~30-120s)
3. Claude reads answer file and discusses with user

No notification endpoint needed - Claude knows to read the answer file when cgpt returns.

**Changes needed:**
1. Add `argument-hint: [draft]` for optional draft-only mode
2. Add step 7 after quality checklist:
   - If $ARGUMENTS starts with "draft", skip automation and just report file location
   - Otherwise, invoke cgpt synchronously, then read answer file and discuss

**Usage:**
- `/ask-question bazel caching` → drafts + sends to ChatGPT + discusses answer
- `/ask-question draft bazel caching` → just drafts file (original behavior)
design:
Simple synchronous flow:
1. Draft question to file (existing logic)
2. Run cgpt -f ... -o ... (blocks ~30-120s)
3. Read answer file
4. Discuss with user

Parse $ARGUMENTS: if first word is "draft", skip steps 2-4 and just report file path.

No verbose status messages needed - just do the work.
close_reason: Updated /ask-question command in dotfiles to invoke cgpt after drafting. Reads answer file and discusses results. Draft mode skips automation.

title: Cancel server work when client disconnects
close_reason: Added AbortController + res.on('close') in handleRequest. Signal passed to queueRequest which skips work if client disconnected before processing starts. Mid-flight operations complete normally (can't cancel Playwright mid-flight). Verified: killed curl during request, server detected disconnect and recovered.

title: Add /research-complete endpoint to Claude-Code-Remote
description:
Add a new HTTP endpoint to Claude-Code-Remote that receives notifications when chatgpt-relay completes a research query. This closes the loop by injecting a message into the Claude Code session.

Endpoint: POST /research-complete

Request body:
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "answer_file": "/tmp/stackexchange-so-answer.md",  // optional
  "source": "chatgpt"
}

Behavior:
1. Validate session_id is provided (400 if missing)
2. Look up session in registry (404 if not found)
3. Construct message:
   - With file: 'Research complete (chatgpt). Answer saved to: /path/to/file'
   - Without file: 'Research complete (chatgpt). Answer copied to clipboard.'
4. Inject message into Claude session via existing injector infrastructure
5. Return {ok: true} or {ok: false, error: '...'}

Location: ~/Code/Claude-Code-Remote/src/channels/telegram/webhook.js (or new route file)

Reference: docs/plans/2026-01-01-chatgpt-relay.md Task 6
design: Reuse existing session registry and injector infrastructure from Claude-Code-Remote. Minor addition - just a new route handler. Could also be a separate routes file if webhook.js is getting large.
close_reason: Implemented /research-complete endpoint in Claude-Code-Remote. Injects notification into Claude session when chatgpt-relay completes.

title: Fix isLoggedIn to require positive evidence of login state
description: The isLoggedIn() function uses negative logic: it assumes logged in unless it finds evidence to the contrary (auth URL or login button). This means ambiguous states (loading, CAPTCHA, redesigned UI) are falsely treated as 'logged in'. Fix: require positive evidence of login (e.g., chat history nav visible) in addition to the absence of login indicators.
notes: Root cause: isLoggedIn used isVisible with 500ms timeout on a SPA page. ChatGPT renders login button via JS after domcontentloaded, so the button wasn't in the DOM yet when we checked. Fix: race loginButton.waitFor vs loggedInIndicator.waitFor with 15s timeout. Whichever appears first determines login state. Neither appearing = not logged in.
close_reason: Added loggedInIndicator selector (chat history nav, prompt textarea, user avatar) and changed isLoggedIn() to require positive evidence. Ambiguous states now correctly return false instead of defaulting to true.

title: Remove wildcard CORS or add auth token
description:
Code review identified a security issue with wildcard CORS.

**Current code in src/server.js handleRequest():**
```javascript
res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', '*');
```

**Problem:** Any webpage you visit can POST to your daemon from the browser (CSRF-from-localhost class). A malicious webpage could send prompts to ChatGPT via your daemon.

**Options:**
1. Remove CORS headers entirely (CLI uses fetch which doesn't need CORS for localhost)
2. Add a random auth token stored in ~/.chatgpt-relay/token, require X-Auth-Token header

Option 1 is simpler and sufficient since this is a local dev tool with no browser UI.

Reference: /tmp/stackexchange-codereview-chatgpt-relay-daemon-answer.md section 4
design: Option 1: Simply remove the three res.setHeader lines for CORS. The CLI's fetch() requests don't trigger CORS checks for same-origin localhost requests.
close_reason: Removed CORS headers entirely - CLI fetch doesn't need them for localhost

title: Implement CLI tool (src/cgpt.js)
description:
Create the main command-line interface that users invoke to send prompts to ChatGPT.

Usage:
  cgpt [options] [prompt]
  cgpt -f question.md -o answer.md
  echo 'question' | cgpt

Options:
  -f, --file <path>     Read prompt from file
  -o, --output <path>   Write response to file
  -s, --session <id>    Claude session ID (auto-detected via session.js)
  -t, --timeout <ms>    Response timeout (default: 120000)
  --new-chat            Start fresh chat instead of reusing tab
  -h, --help            Show help

Behavior:
1. Parse args, get prompt from arg/file/stdin
2. Read WebSocket endpoint from $TMPDIR/cgpt-ws-endpoint (error if missing)
3. Discover Claude session ID via discoverSessionId()
4. Connect to browser server via chromium.connect(wsEndpoint)
5. Call getOrCreateChatGPTPage(), optionally navigateToNewChat()
6. Call sendPromptAndWait() with prompt
7. Output response to stdout
8. If --output: write to file
9. Copy to clipboard via pbcopy
10. If session found: POST to localhost:3001/research-complete

Dependencies: ./session.js, ./chatgpt.js, playwright

Reference: docs/plans/2026-01-01-chatgpt-relay.md Task 5
design: CLI outputs response to stdout, status/progress to stderr. This allows piping. Don't close browser connection on exit - leave server running for next request. pbcopy is macOS-specific but that's our primary target.
close_reason: Implemented CLI with file/stdin input, output to file/stdout/clipboard, auto session discovery, and Claude-Code-Remote notification.

title: Implement ChatGPT DOM automation (src/chatgpt.js)
description:
Create helpers for automating ChatGPT's web interface. This is the fragile part that will need maintenance when ChatGPT's UI changes.

Functions to implement:

1. getOrCreateChatGPTPage(browser)
   - Search all contexts/pages for existing chatgpt.com tab
   - If found, bring to front and return
   - Otherwise create new page and navigate to chatgpt.com

2. navigateToNewChat(page)
   - If not already at root, navigate to https://chatgpt.com/

3. sendPromptAndWait(page, prompt, opts)
   - Find composer (try multiple selectors: #prompt-textarea, textarea, contenteditable)
   - Fill prompt text
   - Click send button (try multiple selectors, fallback to Enter key)
   - Wait for response completion via waitForResponse()

4. waitForResponse(page, timeout) [internal]
   - Poll every 500ms
   - Check for stop button (still generating)
   - Get last assistant message text
   - Return when: no stop button AND text is stable for 1.5s
   - Timeout after opts.timeout (default 120000ms)

Selectors to try (ChatGPT changes these frequently):
- Composer: #prompt-textarea, textarea[data-id=root], textarea[placeholder*=Message]
- Send: button[data-testid=send-button], button[aria-label*=Send]
- Messages: [data-message-author-role=assistant]
- Stop: [data-testid=stop-button], button[aria-label*=Stop]

Reference: docs/plans/2026-01-01-chatgpt-relay.md Task 4
design: Multiple fallback selectors for resilience. Stability-based completion detection (text unchanged for 3 polling cycles). No clicking of ChatGPT's copy button - we extract text directly via textContent(). This is inherently fragile but accepted trade-off.
close_reason: Implemented getOrCreateChatGPTPage, navigateToNewChat, sendPromptAndWait with multiple fallback selectors and stability-based completion detection.

title: Fix overly broad error toast selector and add scoped "Something went wrong" check
description: The div:has-text("Something went wrong") selector matched the entire page body (any ancestor div), causing error messages to include full page innerText dumped into the error. Fixed by: (1) removing the broad selector from errorToast, (2) adding a scoped check in checkErrorStates that looks for "Something went wrong" text within the last assistant turn container only.
close_reason: Fixed alongside P1 work. Removed broad div:has-text selector, added scoped check within assistant turn container.

title: Implement browser server daemon (src/server.js)
description:
Create a long-running Node process that launches Chromium via Playwright's launchServer() API. This keeps the browser alive between CLI requests and persists ChatGPT login.

Key behaviors:
- Launch Chromium with headless: false (user needs to log in)
- Use persistent user-data-dir at ~/.chatgpt-relay/user-data
- Write WebSocket endpoint to $TMPDIR/cgpt-ws-endpoint for CLI discovery
- Handle SIGINT/SIGTERM gracefully, cleaning up endpoint file
- Add --disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled to reduce bot detection

Environment variables for customization:
- CGPT_USER_DATA_DIR: Override profile location
- CGPT_WS_ENDPOINT_FILE: Override endpoint file location

Reference: docs/plans/2026-01-01-chatgpt-relay.md Task 3
design: Using Playwright launchServer() instead of connectOverCDP. This gives higher fidelity than CDP, avoids Chrome 136+ remote debugging restrictions, and provides cleaner lifecycle management. The CLI will use browserType.connect(wsEndpoint) to attach.
close_reason: Implemented browser server with launchServer(), persistent user-data-dir, and WS endpoint file.

title: Verify fetch failure cause with err.cause.code
close_reason: Added err.cause and err.cause.code logging. Next fetch failure will reveal if UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT is the culprit. Also added Undici timeout codes to retry conditions.

title: ProseMirror fill() fragility risk
description: ChatGPT composer is a ProseMirror contenteditable div. Current code uses Playwright .fill() (src/chatgpt.js:189) which can be silently reverted by ProseMirror state reconciliation. Known reliable alternative: document.execCommand('insertText', false, text). Risk is medium -- .fill() works now but could break if OpenAI updates ProseMirror.
close_reason: fill() works with ProseMirror when --disable-gpu is set. The real issue was GPU rendering in background processes, not ProseMirror itself.

title: Tighten bare 'textarea' fallback selector
description:
Code review noted the bare 'textarea' fallback is risky.

**Current code in src/chatgpt.js SELECTORS.composer:**
```javascript
composer: [
  '#prompt-textarea',
  'textarea[data-id="root"]',
  'textarea[placeholder*="Message"]',
  'div[contenteditable="true"][data-placeholder]',
  'textarea'  // <-- This is the problem
].join(', ')
```

**Problem:** On a complex page, bare 'textarea' can match the wrong element (e.g., a feedback form, search box, etc).

**Fix options:**
1. Scope to the message form region: 'form textarea', 'main textarea'
2. Remove the bare fallback entirely (other selectors should be sufficient)
3. Add more specific attribute checks: 'textarea[name*="prompt"]'

The goal is preventing 'random UI change breaks everything' by scoping selectors.

Reference: /tmp/stackexchange-codereview-chatgpt-relay-daemon-answer.md section 3
design: Option 2 is safest - remove the bare 'textarea' fallback. If the specific selectors don't match, we should fail fast rather than type into the wrong element.
close_reason: Removed bare textarea from broad fallback selector

title: Detect dead browser context and recreate browser
description:
**Problem:** When the Chromium browser crashes or is killed, the daemon keeps trying to use the dead browserContext. All subsequent requests fail with:
```
browserContext.newPage: Target page, context or browser has been closed
```

**Current behavior:**
- processRequest() tries `context.newPage()` which fails
- Error is caught, page is set to null
- Next request tries again, same error
- Daemon never recovers

**Expected behavior:**
When browserContext is dead, detect this and recreate the entire browser:
```javascript
if (\!browser || \!browser.isConnected()) {
  console.log('[ask-question-server] Browser disconnected, relaunching...');
  browser = await chromium.launch({...});
  context = await browser.newContext({...});
}
```

**Files:** src/server.js processRequest() and possibly main()

**Alternative:** Exit the daemon when browser dies (let process manager restart it).
close_reason: Added ensureBrowserAlive() that checks browser.isConnected() before each request. If dead, relaunches browser and recreates context with storageState. Extracted browser launch config into getBrowserLaunchOptions() for reuse. Added composer waitFor to processRequest page creation. Verified: killed Chrome processes, next request auto-recovered and succeeded.

title: Fix empty assistant message text (DOM selector issue)
description:
**Problem:** ChatGPT's assistant message selector finds an element (count: 1) but innerText() returns empty string. This causes infinite loop in waitForResponse stabilization.

**Symptoms:**
```
[chatgpt] Empty text, assistant message count: 1
[chatgpt] Empty text, assistant message count: 1
... (repeats forever)
```

**Root cause hypotheses:**
1. ChatGPT changed their DOM structure - the `[data-message-author-role="assistant"]` selector matches but the content is in a child element
2. Content is being rendered in a shadow DOM
3. Content uses a different element structure now

**Investigation needed:**
1. Run in headed mode to inspect the actual DOM
2. Check if content is in a nested element
3. Update selector in src/chatgpt.js SELECTORS.assistantMessage

**Files:** src/chatgpt.js
close_reason: Issue was transient page state corruption, not a selector problem. DOM selectors are correct. Fresh browser restart resolved the issue. The 'empty text' state can occur when the page is in a corrupted state from previous failures - the existing hard reset logic should handle this in most cases.

title: isLoggedIn false-negative on Deep Research / Extended Thinking response pages
description:
checkErrorStates() in src/chatgpt.js calls assertLoggedIn() inside the response stabilization loop (line 569). assertLoggedIn calls isLoggedIn (line 780), which races Playwright waitFor on:
  - nav[aria-label='Chat history']
  - #prompt-textarea
with a 15s timeout. On long Deep Research / Extended Thinking responses, neither selector becomes Playwright-visible during the multi-phase rendering, even though the user is still logged in and the elements ARE in the DOM with non-zero getBoundingClientRect. This is the same bug class fixed in commit 41990f3 for the stop button, where Playwright's CSS-based visibility check is fooled by overlay/opacity but isButtonInDOM (page.evaluate + getBoundingClientRect) succeeds. Result: the relay throws 'Not logged in to ChatGPT. Run ask-question-login first.' AFTER 'Generation complete' is logged. Reliably reproduces with prompts large enough to trigger Deep Research mode (~13.8K char brief). Short prompts (e.g. 2+2) succeed.

Plan: add diagnostic logging first, reproduce, then patch isLoggedIn to fall back to a DOM-level getBoundingClientRect check (mirroring isButtonInDOM) when Playwright visibility races time out. Extend src/chatgpt.test.js to cover the new fallback.
notes:
Root cause confirmed via diagnostic logging in src/chatgpt.js:

[chatgpt] isLoggedIn=false (login-button-won) url=https://chatgpt.com/c/...
[chatgpt]   nav[aria-label=Chat history]: playwrightVisible=true ...
[chatgpt]   #prompt-textarea: playwrightVisible=true ...
[chatgpt]   a[href*=/auth]: playwrightVisible=true dom={"text":"GitHub Docs\\n+1"}

The bug was NOT a Playwright visibility timing issue (initial hypothesis was wrong). It was a false-positive in SELECTORS.loginButton: the broad selector a[href*=/auth] matched citation anchors in deep-research responses (e.g., GitHub Docs links to /auth/* documentation pages). Promise.race in isLoggedIn returned LOGIN_BTN as the winner, so isLoggedIn returned false even though the user was clearly logged in (chat history nav AND prompt textarea both visible).

Fix: removed the broad a[href*=/auth] selector from SELECTORS.loginButton. The URL check at the top of isLoggedIn already detects /auth and login.openai.com redirects, so the anchor selector was redundant. Kept the button:has-text(Log in)/(Sign in) selectors -- they don't false-match because ChatGPT renders citation links as <a>, not <button>.

Also kept the new diagnostic logging in isLoggedIn (best-effort, only fires on the false-return paths) so future selector regressions surface immediately with a screenshot, raw DOM state, and Playwright vs. DOM visibility comparison for each candidate selector.

Tests: added a regression test in src/chatgpt.test.js that asserts the loginButton selector array does not contain a[href*=/auth]. All 7 tests pass.

Verified end-to-end: sent a 13,872-char Deep-Research-triggering prompt through the relay, got back a real 10,312-char ChatGPT answer with citations. Server log shows no isLoggedIn=false entries.
close_reason: Fixed by removing broad a[href*=/auth] selector from SELECTORS.loginButton in src/chatgpt.js. Verified end-to-end with 13.8K char Deep Research prompt; got 10.3K char response. Tests added; all pass.
